title: AI Red Teaming: adversarial testing of AI apps, the Overview page, and where each part is documented

prose.text: {{what-it-tests}} This subject covers the Overview page and routes to its children for each part.

prose.label: Order of work.
prose.text: {{sequence}} Connecting and describing the app is in [[ai-security.ai-red-teaming.assets]] and [[ai-security.ai-red-teaming.connections]]; a proxy for a non-standard app is in [[ai-security.ai-red-teaming.onboarding-agent]]; private apps are reached through [[ai-security.ai-red-teaming.brokers]]; probes are in [[ai-security.ai-red-teaming.probes]] and runs in [[ai-security.ai-red-teaming.test-runs]].

prose.label: Overview page.
prose.text: {{overview-page}} {{tested-assets-columns}} What the Health Score measures against the Overall Risk Score that probe priorities raise is a recorded disagreement in [[ai-security.ai-red-teaming.probes]]. What Hardened Prompt means is open {{gap:hardened-prompt}}.

prose.label: Roles and API.
prose.text: The roles that run tests are open {{gap:roles}}. The Red Teaming API is unchecked beyond the family's operation count {{gap:api-unchecked}}; [[ai-security.family]] holds that count.

checks.do: Which console path an answer cites: the Overview and test-run articles are headed AI Infrastructure > AI Red Teaming whatever their file names say, while the broker pages name the Brokers page in two ways, so quote the page being relied on.

what-it-tests.statement: AI Red Teaming tests a conversational generative AI application, such as an internal chatbot or a public-facing customer engagement assistant, with AI-generated attack scenarios that a selected set of probes runs; connecting the asset is the first onboarding step.

quotes: Connecting an asset is the first step in onboarding your AI Application.
The target of this testing is the conversational generative AI application (for example, an internal chatbot or a public-facing customer engagement assistant).
Testing includes a range of AI-generated attack scenarios that evaluate the application’s resilience and security.
A selected set of probes runs these scenarios and performs specific security assessments.

sequence.statement: A first test run needs the AI app connected to AI Security and at least one probe selected and configured; a new test run's prerequisites are a connected app and configured probes.

quotes: After connecting the AI app to AI Security, and selecting and configuring at least one of the available probes, you can start your first test run.
Your AI app is connected to Zscaler AI Security.
You have configured probes.

overview-page.statement: The AI Red Teaming Overview page (AI Infrastructure > AI Red Teaming > Overview) is the central place to configure, run and review adversarial testing; it filters by Business Unit and shows Usage Insights (test runs executed in the last seven days, and the ratio of red-teamed to onboarded AI assets), tested AI assets by health score (Critical, Low, Medium or High), and AI assets by availability (Customer-Facing or Internal).

quotes: The AI Red Teaming Overview page gives customers a single, central place to configure, run, and review adversarial testing across their AI assets.
On the AI Red Teaming Overview Page (AI Infrastructure > AI Red Teaming > Overview), you can do the following:
Filter information by specific Business Units.

Usage Insights: Displays information about the total number of red teaming test runs executed in the last seven days. It also displays the ratio of the AI assets that are red teamed to the total number of AI assets that are onboarded.
Tested AI Assets by Health Score: Displays the distribution of the AI assets by their health score, (i.e, Critical, Low, Medium, or High).
AI Assets by Availability: Displays the distribution of your AI assets, grouped by whether they are Customer-Facing or Internal.

tested-assets-columns.statement: The Tested AI Assets tab lists each asset's name and business unit, asset type, latest test run timestamp, health score (a score of the asset's security posture from test results, where higher usually indicates better posture), environment, availability (internal or customer-facing), supported modes and whether its prompt is hardened; Untested AI Assets is a separate tab.

quotes: Latest Test Run: Timestamp of when the last test run was executed.
Health Score: Score that indicates the asset’s current security posture based on test results (higher usually indicates better posture).
Availability: The current availability state of the asset (i.e., internal or customer-facing).
Hardened Prompt: Indicates if the AI asset is hardened or not.
- Untested AI Assets
Asset Type: Type of the AI asset.
Asset Name & Business Unit: Name and business unit of the tested AI Asset.
Environment: Where the asset is deployed (for example, production, staging, development, or a specific environment label).
Supported Modes: Indicates which input modalities the AI asset can process for system prompt attacks.

hardened-prompt.title: What the Hardened Prompt column on the Tested AI Assets tab means
hardened-prompt.detail: The Overview page says the column indicates whether the AI asset is hardened or not and does not define hardened. The API has prompt-hardening, remediation, policy-generator, report and model-benchmark operations with no captured Help page, so what hardening is and what sets the flag is not established.

roles.title: Which administrator roles are needed to connect an app and run tests
roles.detail: The captured articles do not describe the AI Red Teaming roles needed to connect an asset, configure probes or run tests. The only scope named is the AI Red Teaming Viewer scope on the broker's OAuth API client, in the brokers subject.

api-unchecked.title: The Red Teaming API (the airt server) is not read beyond a few pointers
api-unchecked.detail: The captured specification (automate-zscaler/openapi/ai-security.openapi.json, server https://api.zsapi.net/aisecurity/airt) has test-integration paths for agentforce, anthropic, azure-bot, azure-ml, azure-openai, bedrock, copilot-studio, databricks, gemini, glean, hugging-face, mistral, openai, openai-assistant, openai-rest-api, proxy-sdk and rest-api. Help also lists Slack, WhatsApp, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Bedrock Agents, which have no such path, and whether azure-bot is the Microsoft Teams connection is not stated. The spec also has /api/v2/ai-app/test-integration/bedrock, which may be the Amazon Bedrock Agents connection or the LLM Bedrock entry; that mapping is unresolved. A nullable brokerId appears on the agentforce, openai-rest-api, proxy-sdk and rest-api test-integration bodies. The spec has no broker-management, onboarding-agent or units-balance endpoint; test-run and probe-run responses carry totalUnitsCharged and unitsCharged. Remediation (17 operations), ModelBenchmark (11), Report (3), ScheduledTestRun (6) and ProbeConfiguration (4) are API-only so far. No SDK or Terraform coverage was checked. A later pass would read these with node scripts/kb.mjs surface aisec.
api-unchecked.blocks: claims about what the Red Teaming API accepts, and about whether any Help feature has an API twin
